title: Dataproc: managed Spark and Hadoop, and when it beats Dataflow

videos.script: Lesson 21 ran a pipeline on Dataflow and never showed you a machine. Dataproc shows you all of them. {{cluster}} A Dataproc cluster is a set of Compute Engine machines in your project, with Spark and Hadoop already installed. Each machine has a role. The master coordinates, primary workers work and store, and secondary workers only work. {{roles}} That difference decides which machines may be Spot, the spare capacity Google sells cheaply and can take back. {{spot}} There is no emulator for Dataproc. But the program a cluster runs is plain Spark, and Spark runs on your laptop. You will run Quitanda's nightly job for real, and check its result with a second engine. {{spark}} Then the money. Per hour of work, a cluster, a Serverless batch and Dataflow cost nearly the same. Left running all month for a two hour job, the cluster costs twelve times what it needed to. {{chart}} By the end you will know when Dataproc beats Dataflow, and when it only looks cheaper. {{end}}
